mechanism: The cued base escapes a forming loop through the head of its distribution, not its tail: a loop locks only when the top-1 token keeps a probability above about 0.9 for a run of positions, so T 1.5 with min-p 0.1 removes loops by flattening the head while still cutting the rare tail, and T 1.0 with min-p 0.1 brings loops back because it sharpens the head, not because it deletes tail tokens.
starts_from: result-44b4df (T 1.0 min-p 0.1: rule-A loops 0 -> 34; T 1.5 + min-p 0.1: 0 loops, 412 right). No graveyard theory explains why a truncating sampler at T 1.5 is loop-free.
differs_from: r3-across-2 (escape needs low-probability tail tokens; any truncation locks loops) predicts the opposite for T 1.5 + min-p, since that sampler also deletes the tail. r2-external-2 and r2-across-1 put the cause in fork entropy at a single temperature and say nothing about head shape under truncation. m02 is about length and correctness, not loops.
first_test: From the min-p cells frustea-1114-180849-456c (T 1.0 min-p 0.1) and -180853-e383 (T 1.5 min-p 0.1), compute n_tok_p_lt_1e2 per 1,000 generated tokens for each answer. Wrong if e383's rate is at least 3x that of 456c's finished answers, or if 456c's looped answers (loop_A) have less than half the rate of its finished answers of matched length; either would mean loop freedom tracks sampled tail tokens. The mechanism predicts e383 at no more than 1.5x 456c's finished rate, and looped and finished answers in 456c within a factor of 1.3.

mechanism: How the cued base's errors relate to length flips sign with difficulty: on easy problems (MATH Levels 1-3) its wrong finished samples are premature commitments, shorter than their right siblings, and on Level 5 they are wandering attempts, longer than their right siblings; RL removes the short premature stops, so its wrong samples are long at every level.
starts_from: r4-m02's refutation (RL within-problem length concordance 0.72, so length reads out failure for RL too) and result-cbe0bc (tie-break by the shortest sample helps the base, +1.4, but not RL). No graveyard theory explains why the shortest-sample rule helps only the base.
differs_from: r4-m02 (base wrong samples are always longer; RL length carries no signal, refuted). r3-surprises-1 (slips add up with length, so wrong samples are longer at every difficulty). m09 is about what a wrong answer contains, not its length.
first_test: Use studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (attempt 0), with level from anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json, restricted to problems with base_k from 1 to 3. For each problem, compute log(n_new of the finished-wrong sample / median n_new of its right siblings). Wrong if the median log-ratio on Levels 1-3 is above 0 (wrong samples longer). It predicts below log 0.9 on Levels 1-3 and above log 1.2 on Level 5. Repeat on math500_rl-01: every level should be above 0.

mechanism: The top-8 singular directions per matrix of the RL-Math delta carry only the mode switch the cue gives (deliberative opening and register), not RL's longer checking policy, so base + top8 on the plain prompt behaves like the cued base: cued-base answer lengths and errors on the problems where the cued base errs.
starts_from: result-ad3c24 and result-36e8cd (top8 plain 427 vs cued base 410, rand8 36/100, top1 42/100; late-MLP top directions read 'Okay'/'Wait'; mean tokens 3,962 against cued base 3,933 and RL 4,694). No graveyard theory explains why 8 directions per matrix are enough.
differs_from: all-2 and r1-all-2 (one diffuse direction that any unbiased fraction flips, so top1 should also work), r1-surprises-2 (the low-rank part carries the deliberation and the answer format, and recovering arms take RL's length), and knowledge-69adda's 'every recovering arm takes RL's length'. This candidate says top8 takes the cued base's length instead. m10 is about the plain base's own openings, not a weight edit.
first_test: Join wsp1/full500/top8_plain-01/per_problem.json (score_v3, n_generated) with rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Wrong if the median n_generated of top8's right answers is at least 2,400 (RL 3,014, cued base 1,432), or if the per-problem Spearman of top8 n_generated with t2_generated_tokens is higher than with t1_generated_tokens. As a second check, top8's wrong set should overlap T1's wrong set beyond the difficulty-matched null of axis/math500-01.

mechanism: Think-SFT's math gain arrives with the looping of a distilled student: imitating long traces from stronger models gives the student a long-horizon structure it cannot sustain, so its gain over the cued base comes on short and medium problems while it runs to the cap on long ones, more often than both the cued base and RL.
starts_from: result-ad3c24 and result-36e8cd (Think-SFT, with no reward, scores 454 with the cue and 440 plain on MATH-500). No graveyard theory explains the imitation delta.
differs_from: r2-across-2 and r2-all-1 (a large, low-coherence SFT delta fails sparse copies; they predict nothing about cap hits), and r4-m10 (cap hits that rise during RL). m03 is about the RL delta's subspace. Unlike m01 and m02, this one makes a claim about the SFT weights themselves.
first_test: Use wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json (score_v3, cap_hit), with quartiles from t2_generated_tokens in t1_t2_items-01. Wrong if Think-SFT has fewer than 27 cap hits (the cued base's count) or fewer than 1.5x RL's T2 cap hits, or if its gain over T1 in the top RL-length quartile is at least half its mean gain in Q1-Q2. It predicts at least 40 cap hits, about half of them in Q4.

mechanism: The base already detects a doubtful step as well as RL does, since hold-on probability rises after a wrong result in both; what RL changed is the action after the hold-on token: after 'Wait' the base re-affirms the value it just had, while RL re-derives it and replaces it, so the base's wrong finished answers keep a value stated before their last 'Wait'.
starts_from: result-c4411d and result-a2dc6f (after a wrong result, hold-on log-prob rises +0.28 in the base and +0.35 in RL, and RL reads partial results no better), together with result-afc423 (base wrong samples are mostly slips and misreads with right siblings).
differs_from: r2-revise-2 (RL has the better error detector, d' 1.1 vs 0.6) and r4-m06 (a constant added bias toward hold-on tokens; extra re-checks change answers at the base's own rate). This candidate puts the difference after the hold-on token, in the revision probability per 'Wait', not in how often 'Wait' appears or how well errors are detected.
first_test: In S3 T1.jsonl (base, cue) and T2.jsonl (RL) text, for each ' Wait'/' Hmm', take the last number or expression stated in the 300 characters before it and the first one stated in the 400 characters after it, and count a revision when they differ. Wrong if the base's revision rate per hold-on is at least 0.8x RL's, or if fewer than 60 % of base finished-wrong answers that contain a hold-on end on a value already stated before their last hold-on. It predicts at most 0.5x RL's rate and at least 70 %.

mechanism: The MATH-500 problems that RL solves but the cued base gets 0 of 4 on lie inside the base's own coverage at a slightly larger k: RL raised the probability of base paths that already exist at a few percent per sample, so the base's other stored samples at other settings solve most of them, and not the problems that RL never solves either.
starts_from: result-afc423 (33 problems at base 0/4 against 0.5 under a homogeneous null; RL solves 17 of them at least once) and result-5da8a9 (0 problems solved only by RL). No graveyard theory explained the 0/4 class.
differs_from: r3-external-2 and r3-across-1 (a dose-scaling part that adds solutions where the base's p is near 0, which predicts that extra base samples do not find them), r4-m07 (wrong-answer attractors, refuted), and m09 (what a wrong answer contains).
first_test: For the 33 base-0/4 problems (anatomy/math500-01/pool_k_le3.json, base_k 0), pool every other stored cued-base sample: r3/base-01 F_math500 (T 0.6, 1-4 samples, v3 recomputed), the min-p and top-p cells 456c, e383 and b614, and the critique drafts. Wrong if 5 or fewer of the 17 problems RL solves at least once (rl_k >= 1) have a right base sample in the pool, or if the pool solves the 16 RL-never problems at the same rate. It predicts at least 10 of 17 against at most 4 of 16.

mechanism: RL step 100 is the base that has learned to open in the cue's register and nothing more: its plain-prompt answers behave like the cued base's, keeping the base's answer format and finished-answer accuracy, so its T 0.6 cap hits rise toward the cued base's 119 because the cued base loops more than the plain base at T 0.6, not because of entropy collapse.
starts_from: r4-m10's survived observation (T 0.6 cap hits: base 65 -> step 100 103 / step 400 98 -> step 2,800 about 16) and knowledge-87618d (step 100 activations are nearly identical to the base's on RL text), set beside result-e870a1 and result-7968b8 (cued base 119 cap hits against 65 for the plain base at T 0.6).
differs_from: r4-m10 (the early steps sharpen the policy and cross top-p's lock threshold). That predicts higher finished-answer accuracy and new loop sites; this one predicts cued-base accuracy and the cued base's own loop sites. It also differs from the untested length-growth rival. m10 is about the plain base, not a checkpoint.
first_test: In r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (plain, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), measure (a) the share of answers that open with ' line'/'!\n\nOkay', (b) the Jaccard of its cap-hit problem set with r3/base-01 F_math500's (cued base) against P_math500's (plain base), and (c) v3 accuracy on finished answers and the 'Answer:' line share. Wrong if the cap-hit overlap with F is not at least 1.3x the overlap with P, or if finished accuracy exceeds F's by more than 5 points, or if the 'Answer:' line share is below 20 %.

mechanism: Revising r3-external-1, which was refuted when Math 3.0 scored 448 with the cue at T 1.0 rather than about 412: masking truncated rollouts did not keep the base's sampler basins; it let Code 3.0 learn its own runaway long generation, the code-task looping seen on LiveCodeBench. On math that generation runs to the cap at T 1.0 on long problems, so Code 3.0's missing math gain (411 vs Code 3.1's 450) is concentrated in the longest problems.
starts_from: result-edceef (Code 3.0 cue 411, +0.2 over the cued base, against Code 3.1 450, although Code 3.0 moved the weights further) and knowledge-9f8067 (64 % of Code 3.0 LiveCodeBench rollouts loop). r4-m09 covered Code 3.1 only; no graveyard theory explains 3.0 against 3.1.
differs_from: r3-external-1 (the masked-truncation release keeps the base's T < 1 basins, a temperature effect) and r4-m09 (Code 3.1 transfers an ending policy). This candidate puts a learned failure in Code 3.0 at T 1.0 and confines it by length. m11 makes a content claim (code-style reasoning) about Code 3.1.
first_test: From axis/math500-01/vectors.json, take the Code 3.0 cue arm and the Code 3.1 cue arm (code_cue), and split problems into quartiles of RL length using t2_generated_tokens. Wrong if less than 50 % of Code 3.1's lead over Code 3.0 lies in the top quartile, or if Code 3.0 trails Code 3.1 by more than 4 problems over Q1-Q2 combined. It predicts at least 60 % in Q4 and a gap within about 3 problems on the shorter half. The same split for Math 3.0 against Math 3.1 should show no Q4 concentration.

mechanism: Many of the cued base's finished-wrong answers on problems it usually solves are short-circuits that box a quantity read off the problem statement (a given number, or an intermediate equal to one) instead of the derived value; RL almost never does this, so this one error type carries much of RL's reliability gain.
starts_from: result-afc423 (base misread 23 %, format 13 %, with 39 of 48 base items with a right sibling being slip/misread/format; first wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer) and the answer_from_problem field in anatomy/judge-01. No graveyard theory explained what the base's sample-specific errors contain.
differs_from: r2-revise-2 (weak error detection), r3-surprises-1 (tail-token slips spread along the answer), r4-m07 (shared wrong attractors, refuted), and r4-m11 (a right answer overwritten after a missed stop). This candidate names one error type that occurs at the commitment step. m02 is about length, not content.
first_test: In studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/judge-01/labels.json, take the base and RL finished-wrong items (planted controls excluded) and compute the answer_from_problem share by model and, for the base, by has_right_sibling. Wrong if the base share is below 15 %, or if the RL share is not at most a third of the base share. It predicts a base share of at least 20 % (higher where there is a right sibling) and an RL share of at most 5 %.

mechanism: With the plain prompt, the base chooses one of two whole modes in its first few tokens: answers that open in the deliberative 'Okay' register on their own solve each problem about as often as cued answers do, and the others fail at the plain rate. So the cue's +38.6 points at T 1.0 is the share of plain answers that do not self-open times that difference, and nothing after the opening matters.
starts_from: knowledge-0b450e (the base opens with '.\n\nOkay' on its own in 168 of 500 plain answers) and knowledge-9e4147 (the cue is worth +38.6 at T 1.0 and plain T 1.0 loses 28 points on short problems).
differs_from: r2-surprises-1 and r2-all-2 (the cue lowers per-token entropy along a continuous surprise axis) and r4-m04 (each answer drawn from one of the two endpoint modes, base or RL, refuted by Wait rates). This candidate is a discrete opening choice inside the base alone. m03 and m07 claim the same mode for a weight edit and for a checkpoint, and each can fail on its own.
first_test: In S3 T3.jsonl (plain base, T 1.0), mark each answer as self-opened if its first 20 tokens contain a newline followed by 'Okay' (or ' line!'), and score with v3. Compare per problem with T1 (cue) in t1_t2_items-01. Wrong if the accuracy of self-opened answers is more than 10 points below T1's on the same problems, or if (1 - self-open share) x (self-opened accuracy - other accuracy) misses the T1 - T3 gap by more than 8 points. It also predicts that, across problems, cue_logprob_base in rln5/map-01/checks.json is higher where T3 self-opens.

mechanism: Code-RL 3.1's math gain is a code-style reasoning habit that its reward amplified (enumerating, simulating loops and checking cases as a program would), which pays on Number Theory and Counting & Probability, where Math-RL instead gains on Intermediate Algebra and Precalculus. The two releases therefore fix different subjects at equal totals.
starts_from: result-4b0d5f and result-e45bf4 (Code-RL 3.1 cue 450 on MATH-500 and 187 on hard328 at 7,613 tokens, far shorter than RL) and result-c9b27e (Math and Code deltas nearly orthogonal). No graveyard theory explains why a code reward raises math.
differs_from: r3-across-1, r3-surprises-2 and r3-all-1 (a shared, domain-general settle-or-commit part that Code and Math both learn), and r4-m09 (Code transfers an ending policy, refuted). This candidate gives Code a content-specific habit and so a second, subject-level axis, against the one-axis reading of result-5da8a9. m08 concerns Code 3.0.
first_test: In the hard328 Code-RL rows (abaybektursun-1114-181216-a619/answers.jsonl), count the answers that contain code blocks, 'def ', 'for i in range' or explicit case-by-case tables, and score them against the rest within RL-length quartiles. On MATH-500 (axis/math500-01), compute code_cue minus rl_cue fix rates on base-wrong problems by subject. Wrong if fewer than 5 % of Code-RL answers show code-style reasoning, or if the Code-minus-Math difference is within ±5 points in every subject. It predicts at least +10 in Number Theory/C&P and at most -10 in Intermediate Algebra/Precalculus.

mechanism: RL models write provisional answer markers (an 'Answer:' line or a box) before they verify, and confirm or replace them later, so first-marker extraction rules such as Wang's (line-start 'Answer:' first, else last box) read the pre-verification value; this costs RL more than it costs the base and explains why Wang found the cue equal to RL 3.0 while v3 shows a 7.6-point gap.
starts_from: result-60d899 (a literal reading of Wang's rule takes the cued base from 405-418 to 336-355) and knowledge-8a31ad (Wang: cue 77.9 against RL 3.0 75.3) beside result-edceef (v3: Math 3.0 cue 448 against cued base 410). No graveyard theory explains the parity.
differs_from: r4-m12 (canonical-form misses on non-integer golds) and r4-m11 (a right answer overwritten by a later marker after a missed stop, a last-marker artifact against the base). This candidate is a first-marker artifact against RL. m09 is about answer content, not extraction.
first_test: Regrade r3/base-01 F_math500 (cued base, T 0.6) and r3/fr-01 F_math500 (3.0 release, cue, T 0.6) texts with v3 and with the literal rule (line-start 'Answer:' first, else last box, else 'Final answer'), on the problems present in both files. Wrong if the literal rule's loss for fr-01 is not larger than its loss for the base, or if fewer than half of fr-01's literal-rule losses have an earlier marker whose value differs from the last box. It predicts the fr-01 loss exceeds the base's by at least 5 points.
